title: Runlet sprint pad — latency/cost microbench
content:
Purpose: super-light, personal sprint sheet to track quick microbench runs (end-to-end) for batching/quantization/kv-cache warmup hypotheses. Not a polished runbook — notes to self + quick CSV table for copy/paste into analysis notebook.

Hypotheses:
- H1: int4 quant + aggressive batching yields ~2.5x token cost reduction with <1.6x p95 latency increase for short sequences (<64).
- H2: prefix/KV cache warmup (first 2 requests) skews p95; need to exclude first warmup window for steady-state numbers.
- H3: small model-variant fallback (fp16 -> int8) should reduce tail latency under cold-start by maintaining smaller memory pressure.

Quick run notes (ops):
- config used: model=redwood-7b-v2, hw=gpu-A100-80GB, runtime=rt-2026-02, kernel=auto-select
- metrics collection: local bench harness (./bench/runlet) + console traces (route=/v1/streams), aggregate via small pandas script.
- cost: rough token price used for calc = $0.0009 / 1k tokens for fp16 baseline, quant modifier estimated (int4 -> 0.42x).
- warmup policy: first 2 requests = warmup; exclude for steady-state unless marked otherwise.

CSV: run_id,date,model,quant,batch_size,tokens_per_request,avg_latency_ms,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,cost_per_1k_tokens,notes
R-001,2025-11-07,redwood-7b-v2,fp16,1,32,28.7,22.5,48.2,102.1,0.0009,"baseline, cold start included"
R-002,2025-11-07,redwood-7b-v2,int8,1,32,25.4,20.1,39.7,85.6,0.00038,"int8 quant, single request"
R-003,2025-11-08,redwood-7b-v2,int4,4,32,46.1,35.2,78.9,145.3,0.000378,"batch=4, int4, lower cost but tail latency up"
R-004,2025-11-08,redwood-7b-v2,int4,8,32,82.9,68.4,155.2,330.4,0.00034,"batch=8, queueing visible at p95+, throughput good"
R-005,2025-11-09,redwood-7b-v2,fp16,8,32,60.2,52.1,120.3,250.1,0.0009,"fp16 batch=8 for comparison"
R-006,2026-02-25,redwood-7b-v2,int4,4,8,22.8,19.0,37.5,79.2,0.00038,"short seq(8) steady-state, wins on both latency & cost"
R-007,2026-03-01,redwood-7b-v2,int4+kvcache,4,32,39.5,33.2,64.1,118.7,0.00038,"kv cache warm -> removes prefix cost; exclude first two requests"

Quick observations (raw):
- Excluding warmup, int4 batch=4 looks best cost/latency for short inputs. R-006 shows int4 dominates when seq len small.
- Larger batches (8) introduce tail due to queueing; need adaptive batch thresholds based on p95 SLO.
- KV cache dramatically helps when repeated prefixes; measure % of cache hits in trace (target >90% for this workload).

Action items / TODOs (short):
- [ ] Run R-006 style sweep across 7b/13b to verify scale-up behavior (linear or superlinear tail?). Ticket: RED-314.
- [ ] Add binary flag in bench harness to automatically strip first N warmup requests from aggregates.
- [ ] Try int4 with per-layer fallback (some layers int8) — small custom kernel; open PR to runtime.
- [ ] Add quick annotation in Console to flag runs with warmup included.

Notes-to-self (fragments):
- When summarizing for product: present tradeoff as "cost per 1k tokens vs p95 latency" scatter + clear warmup exclusion note.
- For Dedicated customers, recommend conservative default: int8 + batch <=4 unless workload proves small token lengths.
- Remember to check GPU memory fragmentation on long-lived pods (observed small OOMs on longer experiments).

References / links:
- linear RED-314 (sweep 7/13b): https://linear.app/RED-314
- runtime PR (kernel selection tweak): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/888
- Slack thread: #infra-bench "int4 noise" (search term: int4 noise 2025-11)

End — quick log for sprint day. Will paste CSV into notebook for plots and adjust TODOs after next run.

— noelle
